caption: Israel Mikel v. Commissioner; Erna Mikel v. Commissioner (consolidated)

source.document_title: MEMORANDUM OPINION, JUDGE LAUBER T.C. MEMO. 2015-64 (AN APPROPRIATE ORDER WILL BE ISSUED)

posture: Cross-motions for partial summary judgment (facts deemed established for the motions).

found_facts.fact: Notice determined against each petitioner a deficiency and a 6651(a)(1) addition
found_facts.snippet: determined against each petitioner a tax deficiency of $268,950 and a late-filing addition to tax under section 6651(a)(1) of $67,238.

found_facts.fact: Each spouse's 2007 gift to the trust
found_facts.snippet: During 2007 each petitioner made to a family trust a gift with an asserted value of $1,631,000.

each petitioner claimed under section 2503(b) an annual exclusion of $720,000. The claimed annual exclusions of $720,000 were based on the contention that each petitioner's gift included a $12,000 gift of a present interest to each of the trust's 60 beneficiaries.

found_facts.fact: Gift-splitting consent; no gift tax reported after unified credit
found_facts.snippet: The Forms 709 included consents by each petitioner that the gifts were to be "considered as made one-half by each of [us]." ... After application of unified credits, the Forms 709 reported no gift tax due.
for gifts made during 2007, the exclusion was $12,000 per donee. Rev. Proc. 2006-53, sec. 3.32
Neither petitioner timely filed Form 709 ... for 2007. On December 15, 2011, after being contacted by the IRS, each petitioner submitted a separate Form 709

issue: Whether the gifts to the trust were gifts of present interests (Crummey withdrawal rights) qualifying for the sec. 2503(b) annual exclusion, given an in terrorem clause and a beth din arbitration provision.
holding: Present interests; petitioners' motion for partial summary judgment granted, respondent's denied. Each beneficiary held a legally enforceable withdrawal right. The exact number of beneficiaries was left open (fn. 2: 'not material to this opinion'); valuation not at issue.

recomputation.what: Deficiency = gift tax on 1,631,000 with no exclusions, minus gift tax on 1,631,000 - 720,000 (zero after unified credit); assumes no prior taxable gifts (opinion mentions none).
steps: gift tax with exclusions disallowed = 614,750 - 345,800 = 268,950 == stated deficiency
with 60 x 12,000 = 720,000 exclusions: taxable gift 911,000 < 1,000,000 -> tax 0 (matches 'no gift tax due')
recomputation.court_outcome_effect: Holding sustains the exclusions in principle, so the deficiency falls to 0 if 60 present-interest donees are established (number left open).

judgment: legal question: present vs future interest (enforceability of Crummey right)
number of beneficiaries not finally resolved
computation: taxable gift, tentative tax, unified credit, late-filing addition

caveats: Summary-judgment opinion; final decision figures are not in the opinion.
Assumes no pre-2007 taxable gifts; opinion is silent.
